proposal.utterance: Consideration is a disposition realized in the formation process.

entities.label: Consideration
entities.rationale: Consideration in contract law is an internally grounded capacity of a legal act or party — it disposes that act toward legal enforceability. BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016) models internally grounded tendencies that may or may not be realized; consideration fits this because it is a property of an offer/promise that grounds the possibility of binding contract formation, independently of whether formation actually occurs.

entities.label: ContractFormationProcess
entities.rationale: Contract formation is a temporal process (an occurrent) during which an agreement comes into existence. BFO Process (BFO_0000015) is the correct type for any happening that unfolds in time. The user's utterance refers to 'the formation process', grounding this as a class of legal processes.

relations.rationale: BFO_0000054 (realized in) links a Disposition or Role to the Process in which it is realized. The user asserts that consideration (a disposition) is realized in the formation process, so this predicate captures that claim exactly. Note: in BFO, BFO_0000054 holds between an instance of a realizable entity and an instance of a process; at the class level this is expressed as a range/domain constraint or a subclass axiom with existential restriction. We record it here as a class-level relation to be expanded to an OWL restriction (∃ BFO_0000054 some ContractFormationProcess) on Consideration.

BFO_0000055 (realizes) is the inverse of BFO_0000054, asserting that the ContractFormationProcess class realizes Consideration dispositions. Including both directions makes the inverse relation explicit for the reasoner.

proposal.rationale_summary: The user's utterance asserts that consideration is a disposition — an internally grounded realizable entity — that gets realized in the process of contract formation. BFO_0000016 (Disposition) is the correct type because consideration is a property intrinsic to a legal act or party's offer that grounds enforceability, not merely an externally assigned role. Two new classes are proposed: 'Consideration' as a subclass of BFO Disposition, and 'ContractFormationProcess' as a subclass of BFO Process. proposal.utterance: A breach of contract is a process that disrupts the enduring obligation relation.

entities.label: BreachOfContract
entities.rationale: A breach of contract is a kind of happening or event that unfolds in time — it is an occurrent process, not a continuant. The utterance explicitly classifies it as a process.

entities.label: ContractualObligationRelation
entities.rationale: The 'enduring obligation relation' refers to the contractual obligation that persists between parties — best modeled as a subclass of LegalObligation (which is already typed as a Role/SDC). The relational character is captured by the Role typing, which is externally grounded in the contractual relationship. This is 'enduring' because it persists as a specifically dependent continuant in the bearer across time until discharged or breached.

entities.label: ObligationDisruption
entities.rationale: The 'disruption' of the obligation relation is a quality or change-of-state property that characterizes the post-breach condition of the obligation. It inheres in the bearer of the obligation and marks the alteration effected by the breach process.

relations.rationale: ContractualObligationRelation is a specialization of LegalObligation, inheriting its Role/SDC typing and adding the contractual grounding.
BreachOfContract is explicitly typed as a Process (BFO_0000015) per the utterance.

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance introduces three ontological commitments: (1) that specific performance is a kind of process (a happening unfolding in time), (2) that it is specifically a remedy-process (a process whose purpose is legal restoration), and (3) that it stands in a realization relation to a LegalObligation — namely, the process realizes (BFO_0000055) the obligation that was left unfulfilled. I mint SpecificPerformance and RemedyProcess as new Process subclasses, and ObligationRealization as a Process subclass naming the target of the realization relation. The existing working:LegalObligation (typed as BFO_0000023 Role) is reused as the object of the realizes relation, consistent with BFO's model where a Role is realized in a Process. The subclass chain SpecificPerformance ⊑ RemedyProcess ⊑ BFO_0000015 and SpecificPerformance ⊑ ObligationRealization capture the composite claim that the remedy-process is simultaneously a restoration of the obligation's being-realized.
